questions.text:
Assume that multiplying a matrix G1 of dimension pxq with another matrix G2 of
dimension pxq requires pqr scalar multiplications. Computing the product of n  matrices G1G2G3...Gn can be done by parenthesizing in different ways. Define Gi Gi+1 as an explicitly computed pair for a given paranthesization if they are directly multiplied. For example, in the matrix multiplication chain G1G2G3G4G5G6 using parenthesization (G1(G2G3))(G4(G5G6)), G2G3 and G5G6 are the only explicitly computed pairs. Consider a matrix multiplication chain F1F2F3F4F5, where matrices F1, F2, F3, F4 and F5 are of dimensions 2x25, 25x3, 3x16, 16x1 and 1x1000, respectively. In the parenthesization of F1F2F3F4F5 that minimizes the total number of scalar multiplications, the explicitly computed pairs is/are
questions.solution:
Dimensions 2, 25, 3, 16, 1, 1000. Because [latex]F_4[/latex] has 1 column, it pays to collapse [latex]F_1..F_4[/latex] into a 2 [latex]\times[/latex] 1 matrix first, then multiply by [latex]F_5[/latex]:
[latex]F_3F_4[/latex]: 48 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]F_2(F_3F_4)[/latex]: 75 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]F_1(\ldots)[/latex]: 50 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex](\ldots)F_5[/latex]: 2000. Total 2173, the minimum.

The only pair of original matrices multiplied directly is [latex]F_3F_4[/latex].

Answer: F3F4 only

Second loop: j = 40 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 20 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 5 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1, adding 1 each time j [latex]\gt[/latex] 1: 5 times.

questions.text:
Consider the unsigned 8-bit fixed point binary Number System below,

[latex]b_7 b_6 b_5 b_4 b_3 . b_2 b_1 b_0[/latex]

where the position of the binary point is between [latex]b_3 \; and \; b_2[/latex]. Assume [latex]b_7[/latex] is the most significant bit. Some of the decimal numbers listed below cannot be represented exactly in the above representation:

(i) 31.500 (ii) 0.875 (iii) 12.100 (iv) 3.001

Which one of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
5 integer bits and 3 fraction bits: representable values are multiples of 1/8 = 0.125 from 0 to 31.875.
- 31.5 True, 0.875 = 7/8 True
- 12.1 and 3.001 are not multiples of 1/8 False

Answer: Only (iii) and (iv) cannot be exactly represented

options: None of (i), (ii), (iii), (iv) can be exactly represented
Only (iii) and (iv) cannot be exactly represented
Only (i) and (ii) cannot be exactly represented

questions.text:
The size of the physical address space of a processor is [latex]2^{P}[/latex] bytes. The word length is [latex]2^{W}[/latex] bytes. The capacity of cache memory is [latex]2^{N}[/latex] Bytes. The size of each cache block is [latex]2^{M}[/latex] words. For a K-way set-associative cache memory, the length (in number of bits) of the
tag field is
questions.solution:
Address = P bits. A K-way cache of [latex]2^N[/latex] bytes has [latex]2^N/K[/latex] bytes per way, so set index + block offset = [latex]N-\log_2K[/latex] bits.

Tag = [latex]P-(N-\log_2K)=P-N+\log_2K[/latex]

Answer: [latex]P-N+\log_2K[/latex]

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

questions.text:
Consider the following languages:

I. [latex] \{a^{m}b^{n}c^{p}d^{q}|m+p=n+q, \; where \; m,n,p,q \geq 0 \}[/latex]
II. [latex]\{a^{m}b^{n}c^{p}d^{q}|m=n \; and \; p=q, \; where \; m,n,p,q\geq 0 \} [/latex]
III. [latex] \{a^{m}b^{n}c^{p}d^{q}|m=n=p \; and \; p\neq q, \; where \; m,n,p,q\geq 0 \} [/latex]
IV. [latex]\{a^{m}b^{n}c^{p}d^{q}|mn=p+q, \; where\; m,n,p,q\geq 0\}[/latex]

Which of the languages above are context-free?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: m + p = n + q needs only one counter (a's and c's add, b's and d's subtract) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True
- II: [latex]a^mb^mc^pd^p[/latex]: two independent matches in sequence [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True
- III: m = n = p needs three equal counts [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not CFL
- IV: mn = p + q needs multiplication [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not CFL

Answer: I and II only
